newsitem.title: UK: London gold slips to 4-1/4 year low fixing.
newsitem.headline: London gold slips to 4-1/4 year low fixing.

text.p: Gold prices slid to the lowest fixing since March 30, 1993 on Monday as a thin market came under fresh selling pressure, dealers said.
Bullion was fixed at $334.05 per ounce, down from $336.55 on Friday afternoon, which was the lowest fix since April 1, 1993.
Dealers said pockets of buying had slowed the fall, but even weaker prices were forecast.
The slide began in New York on Friday, when speculative commodity funds began to unload gold from their portfolios on to a reluctant market.
Part of the reason for the funds selling and the general lack of interest in bullion was the firming U.S. dollar and more attractive returns to be gained from the soaring stock markets.
Dealing in the early part of this week would be limited by the meeting of the U.S. monetary policy advisory group the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).
Despite the soaring equities market and thriving U.S. economy, economists have forecast the FOMC advising no change in interest rates.
"That suggests there will be no brake put on the stock market so gold can expect to be ignored," one dealer said.
Another noted that the market could be in the early months of a two-three year bear market.
"We are not going to get the big speculative long buying while there are central banks wondering what to do with their gold reserves," he noted.
The target price for gold in the current wave was $326 per ounce, a level last seen in early March 1993, when gold fell to its lowest price in seven years.
The next level was the March 1985 low of $287.25.
"Once the $326 level is broken the next low will be $315/$316 then the $287," a dealer said.
If the first figure held, there was a chance the price would bounce modestly, he added.
"Then we can expect to see the produers flattening the rally as they try to lock in prices before the next fall," he said.
Business was light across the precious metals markets as Hong Kong was closed for the territory's transfer back to Chinese rule.
Silver followed gold lower at $4.71/$4.73, down two cents, but platinum was $12 dearer at $422.00/$427.00 and palladium was $3.00 easier at $189.00/$194.00.
